standard_prerequisites.name: The equivalence between localized sheaves and slices
standard_prerequisites.use: Identifies the lower shriek with the projection from the slice, which is then compared.

standard_prerequisites.name: The description of the lower shriek on presheaves
standard_prerequisites.use: Gives the alternative direct argument, since sheafification is exact.

core_obligations: Reduction to the slice (proof lines 5632-5636): under the equivalence identifying the localized category of sheaves with the slice, and since equivalences commute with limits, the assertion reduces to the corresponding commutation property of the projection from the slice.

Alternative direct argument (proof lines 5636-5641): the author records that one may instead use the description of the lower shriek on presheaves together with the exactness of sheafification, and that in the case where the site has fibre products and equalizers the result also follows from a companion lemma.
proof_roadmap: Use the equivalence with the slice to reduce to the projection from the slice.
Alternatively use the description of the lower shriek and exactness of sheafification.
Conclude the assertion and the consequence for subsheaves.
difficulty_reason: The lemma states that the lower shriek along a localization commutes with fibre products and equalizers, hence with finite connected limits, and consequently preserves inclusions of sheaves (statement lines 5622-5629). The proof is a short reduction: the equivalence between the localized category of sheaves and the slice identifies the functor with the projection from the slice, and since equivalences commute with limits the assertion becomes the corresponding commutation property of that projection (proof lines 5632-5636); the author also records a direct argument through the description of the lower shriek and the exactness of sheafification, and a further alternative when the site has fibre products and equalizers (proof lines 5636-5641). The non-formal content is the identification with the projection from a slice. The claim is H1: a two-step reduction with alternatives named.
